claims.statement: For F=a(W)+h(X)b(W) with disjoint physical blocks and a+b,a-b Boolean, every adaptive tree complete on X satisfies sum over source-query nodes w_v R_v <= J(a,b;h), even when W and X queries are arbitrarily interleaved.
For the one-bit selector interface with arbitrary Boolean source of mean p, every adaptive interleaving satisfies sum_source w_v R_v<=Q(p)<=8p ln2<=32 ln2 I(d).
The exact two-state disjoint activation decrement depends on the Boolean source only through its mean and variance and is a sum of feasible nonnegative scalar kernels.
